g.text: Safety: what a tool call passes through
The gates are checked in order, and the first that decides wins. The output is cleaned on its way back to the model.
1 the floor: rm -rf /, mkfs, force-push to main
3 taint: text copied from a web page or MCP
6 the mode: plan, default, acceptEdits, yolo
the floor holds in every mode,
in the chat, in a git repository: a snapshot first,
so /undo can put the files back
commands never get Amness's own API keys
web and MCP output is marked as
no tools reads untrusted text first
Defense in depth, not a guarantee: the floor matches patterns in the command text. The sandbox is what enforces limits.
